proposed_reason: Sharp coherent dog portrait: attached anatomy, resolved eyes/muzzle and natural fur texture.
Difficult gymnast pose remains anatomically connected to the apparatus with resolved edges and no fusion.
Two skiers and their skis/poles remain separately readable; small scale alone is not a defect.
Full dog body is coherent and adequately sharp for this model's class band.
Small skiers and equipment are coherent; ordinary distance-related detail loss is acceptable.
Sleeping pose and shallow-focus softness are visible, but face/body boundaries remain coherent and the softness is not clearly below the class band.
Portrait has modest low-resolution softness while eyes, muzzle and fur boundary remain readable.
Oversaturated painterly rendering is imperfect but does not erase anatomy or fuse subject parts.
Body proportions are slightly unusual yet still plausible, attached and not clearly malformed.
Old-photo softness is present, but the dog silhouette, limbs and face remain sufficiently coherent for a boundary/mild call.
Strong global smoothing produces a plastic face and erases normal fur/facial detail: recognizable subject does not make this quality-normal.
Eyes and head contour are visibly blurred/melted below the ordinary class band.
Global blur removes facial and fur structure despite the dog remaining recognizable.
Severe global blur and body/background fusion materially degrade the whole subject.
Gymnast and apparatus are grossly stretched and fused; this is a clear fusion failure, not a hard-but-valid pose.
Hind limbs merge and attach incorrectly, producing an unmistakable topology/misalignment defect.
Gymnast limbs are duplicated/incoherent around the bars.
A ski-like object floats detached high above the people and slope.
Dog anatomy is grossly fused/duplicated with incompatible body parts.
Gymnast arms are missing/fused into symmetric blobs rather than valid articulated limbs.
